what_this_is: W08b lesson bodies (C13): the eight lessons that unlocked both records of a W08b merge pair now teach one point. Exact-substring replacements measured on the post-merge body; every example and fact kept.
fold_rule: verdict keyed by the row's stable identity: ok -> the authored text; corrected -> the verifier's text (authored text kept as authored_*); rejected -> `held`, never applied
apply_contract: per lesson, in table order, per span: body.count(from) == count, then body = body.replace(from, to). A span whose `from` is gone (and whose `to` is present, when non-empty) is already applied. Both layers: research/derived/lessons/<slug>.json body and localized_text(lesson, body, pt-BR).

authored_header.status: pending: nothing applied. Spans are measured on the POST-MERGE body, so apply after migrate_grammar_merge.py has rewritten the loser addresses (and after w08b_merges.json reconciled_prose), never before.
authored_header.source: research/derived/pending/w08b_merges.json (merges[].loser/winner); lesson bodies read at git HEAD 97550c2a (working tree identical for all eight)
authored_header.apply_contract: Per lesson, in row order: body.count(old_span) == 1, then body = body.replace(old_span, new_span). Rows of one lesson never overlap (checked sequentially). Apply to research/derived/lessons/<slug>.json body and to the DB localized_text(lesson, body, pt-BR) the same way the merge rewrote them; if old_span is absent, stop: the body moved.
method: Found each lesson as the one whose unlocks carry both gram:<loser> and gram:<winner> at HEAD: exactly one per pair.

Built the post-merge body by the exact rewrite migrate_grammar_merge.plan_lesson_bodies performs (ref="gram:<loser>" and item-ref="gram:<loser>" -> survivor), then read every place the loser used to sit.

Edited only where the merged body now presents one record as two: a chip described as a different thing than the same chip elsewhere (U1, D2, D5, D7, D8, D10), a list entry repeating another (D4), and the checklist, where each former record had its own row with the same item-ref after the merge (all eight; merged into one row keeping every clause).
Kept form subsections (ちゃう／じゃう in D7, んだもん in D10, sentido 1/2 in D7, quantities in U1) as subsections of one point: they teach forms and uses, not a second record.

Self-check (scratch build.py): every old_span occurs exactly once in the post-merge body and still once after the lesson's earlier rows; no loser key in any span; no em/en dash in new text; scripts/validate/validate_lessons.LessonParser reports no error on the edited body that it did not already report on the unedited one.
